comment: Brian (ElevenLabs) VO for the 300s Match 14 video — France vs Senegal, Group I, Matchday 1, SoFi Stadium, Los Angeles. Series episode 14. On-canon with content/Stories/France-vs-Senegal.md ('The Empire and the Lion'). REAL history: the two nations have met only ONCE that mattered — the 2002 World Cup opening match, when Senegal, a former French colony, beat the reigning world champions France 1-0 (Papa Bouba Diop, 30'), one of the greatest upsets ever. The ending here is OUR PREDICTION (a 1-1 draw built on the Story's 56th-minute Mbappe-vs-Mane sequence), explicitly labelled as a prediction. `at` = start time in seconds; mux.mjs time-fits lines to their slots. SOCCER ONLY.

lines.text: Listen. One goal. One night in two thousand and two... and the champions of the world fell to a country they once ruled.
Tonight, the empire and the lion meet again. And the ghosts of that night... are still watching.
Welcome back to WorldCup twenty-six Legends — episode fourteen. France versus Senegal. Group I. SoFi Stadium, Los Angeles.
Seventy thousand fans under the cathedral of American sport. The blue of France, the green of Senegal... and a wound that never fully healed.
These two nations have met only once where it truly mattered. The opening match of the two thousand and two World Cup. France: reigning world champions, reigning European champions, untouchable.
Senegal: a former French colony, playing in their very first World Cup, with a squad raised in the French leagues. Nobody gave them a prayer.
Thirtieth minute. Papa Bouba Diop bundles the ball over the line... and the unthinkable is real. Senegal one, France nil. The colony had humbled the empire.
France went home without scoring a single goal. Senegal marched to the quarter-finals. That night became a symbol — of African football, and of defiance.
Twenty-four years later, France are champions again, and Senegal are kings of Africa. The rematch the world has waited a generation for... is finally here.
So meet tonight's France. The most feared attacking machine on Earth. Three names carry the storm.
Kylian Mbappe. The Prince of Bondy. Real Madrid's number ten. Thirty-eight kilometres an hour of pure intent — a man who scored a hat-trick in a World Cup final... and still lost.
Beside him, Ousmane Dembele — two feet, no weakness, a dribble that ties defenders in knots and a Ballon d'Or in his hands.
And anchoring it all, Aurelien Tchouameni — the metronome who decides the tempo of the game before the game even begins.
But Senegal are no underdogs now. Champions of Africa. The Lions of Teranga. They have already proven, once, that a French passport on the team sheet means nothing when the heart belongs to Dakar.

Sadio Mane. The King of Teranga. The Dakar Express. His nation's greatest ever scorer — a man who walked four hundred kilometres for a dream, then built his village a hospital, a school and a mosque with the reward.
Nicolas Jackson — the blade on the counter, all sprint and ice, waiting for one Mbappe mistake.
And Kalidou Koulibaly, the captain, the wall — the calm that turns panic into order.
Every great match hides a duel inside it. The Prince... against the King. Mbappe's lightning against Mane's relentless, ageless will. Speed versus soul.
One of them bends this night to his name. The other carries the weight of two thousand and two on his back.
Our storytellers have looked into tonight... and this is what they saw. Remember — it is a prediction, not a result.
Fifty-sixth minute. Mbappe receives on the left and explodes — that burst that has buried the best defenders alive. He cuts inside, and he strikes.
GOAL! France lead! The Prince silences seventy thousand souls, and for a moment the empire stands tall again.
Blue smoke, blue joy. But watch the man in green refuse to drop his head.
Mbappe runs again — and this time, at thirty-four years old, Mane tracks every stride, and slides, and wins the ball clean. The crowd cannot believe his legs.
He springs up, drives, slips it to Jackson on the break — and the equaliser flies in! GOAL Senegal! The lion roars in Los Angeles!
Full time, in our story: one, all. Not the upset of two thousand and two... but proof the lion still hunts the empire as equals.
A point each. A goal for the Prince, a goal for the King. Group I left wide open, exactly as the storytellers like it.
And that is the beauty of it. Nothing decided. Everything still to play for.

But before you go — every nation in our story hides a legend. Senegal's is the Lion of Goree. An old griot who has drummed at every match since the great upset, his rhythm said to carry the ancestors onto the pitch.
Tonight... they say the drum was heard. Collect the Lion of Goree — and forty-seven more legends — inside the game.
Now here is where YOU come in. Did you see this coming? At WorldCup twenty-six dot world, you pick three of the forty-eight nations — and every single goal they score... scores for you.
Underdogs multiply your points. The leaderboard moves live with every goal. And it is completely free to play. Your three picks could change everything.

If this story moved you, send it to the friend who still thinks Africa cannot stand toe to toe with Europe. Like, subscribe... because next, Spain begin their hunt — and the storytellers have already seen the ending.
